title: Wire the assimilate workflow as a shipped skill: skills/hivemind-assimilate-skill
description: Phase G-3 (addon surface). Author the orchestrator-facing WIRED skill that operationalizes addon-packs.md §4/§7 and addon-packs-plan.md §7/§12 — the surface the design docs name `hivemind-assimilate-skill`. It ships under plugin-root skills/ (parity-copied to .claude/skills/ in the dev repo) so an orchestrator in ANY hivemind project loads it via progressive disclosure and knows the third-party-skill adoption protocol. The skill drives pack-ctl (TASK-135) for the deterministic steps (classify/scan/stage), spawns the REAL security-reviewer subagent over the fetched content (incl. its instruction text for prompt-injection), assembles the approval package, requires explicit human sign-off, then stages + reconciles via pack-ctl. No source logic — this is a SKILL.md + sensor wiring. Depends on TASK-135.
acceptance_criteria: skills/hivemind-assimilate-skill/SKILL.md exists with a progressive-disclosure description stating WHEN to load (adopting a third-party Agent Skill / design-pack resource) and the full human-gated flow: fetch+pin -> license classify -> scan -> security-reviewer subagent verdict -> approval package -> explicit human sign-off -> stage -> reconcile-apply.
The skill instructs driving pack-ctl for the deterministic ops and spawning the security-reviewer subagent for the verdict — explicitly NOT running license/safety judgement inside the CLI.

It states the locked invariants verbatim in intent: no third-party skill adopts without an explicit human approve (license classification is decision-support only, forgeable); a suspicious verdict blocks even approve unless the human passes an explicit override; assimilation never goes autonomous under any loop_auth grant.
Skill parity + manifest-skills sensors updated so the new skill is covered and green (agents-parity.spec.js / manifest-skills.spec.js / any skills-parity doc-lock).
A dev-repo .claude/skills/hivemind-assimilate-skill parity copy exists so the parity sensor passes.

comments.author: uat
comments.body:
UAT (verified by Orchestrator at the human's request — uat_delegated_to_orchestrator standing grant). Script derived from the 5 ACs; every AC covered, all steps PASS.

Step 1 (AC1) — Run: inspect skills/hivemind-assimilate-skill/SKILL.md frontmatter + body. Expect: a `description:` stating WHEN to load (third-party skill adoption) + the ordered human-gated flow. Observed: description names the trigger conditions ("assimilate a skill", "vendor this skill", pack-ctl assimilate, integrations.lock.json, assimilated-skills/) and the full flow (fetch+pin -> license classify -> scan -> security-reviewer verdict -> approval package -> human sign-off -> stage -> reconcile); 51 ordered-flow keyword hits. Live signal: the skill auto-loaded into the orchestrator session with this description via progressive disclosure. PASS.

Step 2 (AC2) — Run: grep the flow for the tool boundary. Expect: deterministic ops driven via pack-ctl; license/safety JUDGEMENT (security-reviewer subagent + human) OUTSIDE the CLI. Observed: 7 pack-ctl/dist references + 9 security-reviewer/subagent/spawn references + 7 explicit "outside / network-free / judgement" boundary statements. PASS.

Step 3 (AC3) — Run: grep for the locked invariants. Expect: (a) no adoption without explicit human approve; (b) license classification decision-support only + forgeable; (c) suspicious verdict blocks even approve unless explicit override; (d) never autonomous under any loop_auth grant. Observed: 19 invariant-language hits; reviewer independently cross-checked all four against src/assimilate.js (L291/L322) + addon-packs.md §4/§7 and found them FAITHFUL (no HIGH). PASS.

Step 4 (AC4) — Run: npx vitest run tests/assimilate-skill.spec.js. Expect: a byte-identity parity sensor green. Observed: 4 passed (exists + frontmatter + dev copy exists + byte-identical); red-green planted by the developer (fails on a 1-byte corruption). PASS.

Step 5 (AC5) — Run: diff the two SKILL.md copies. Expect: .claude/skills/ dev parity copy exists byte-identical. Observed: diff -> no output (IDENTICAL). PASS.

Overall: PASS (5/5). The flag contract documented in the skill was independently verified by the reviewer against bin/pack-ctl.js ASSIMILATE_FLAG_SPEC (no fabricated flags; strict override semantics correct).
